questions.question: Who was the author of the book ‘Gulamgiri’ ?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: 'C) Jyotirao Phule.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotirao Phule authored the book *Gulamgiri* (Slavery).**

 
 
• *Gulamgiri* was published in 1873 and is considered one of the seminal works in Indian social reform literature.
 
• The book critiques the caste system and draws parallels between the slavery experienced by African Americans and the oppression of lower castes in India.
 
• Phule dedicated the book to the American abolitionist movement, highlighting the universal struggle against social injustices.
 
• It advocates for the upliftment of oppressed communities through education and social reform.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Incorrect Statements__**

__
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati:**

 
 
• Dayanand Saraswati was a social reformer and founder of the Arya Samaj, but he did not author *Gulamgiri.*
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda:**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda was a spiritual leader and social reformer who worked for social equality, but he did not write *Gulamgiri.*
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy:**
 
 
• Raja Rammohan Roy, a pioneer of modern Indian reform, is known for his efforts to abolish practices like sati but was not the author of *Gulamgiri.*
 
 

**Hence, the correct option is: C) Jyotirao Phule.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Jyotirao Phule:**__

 __
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a social reformer from Maharashtra who worked tirelessly for the rights of marginalized communities, especially Dalits and women.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, championed the cause of education for the oppressed and established the first school for girls in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of *Gulamgiri*:**__
 
 
• The book exposed the deep-rooted inequalities of the caste system and advocated for social justice and equality.
 
• It served as a call to action for reformers to challenge entrenched social hierarchies.

questions.question: Which of the following lacks membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viruses**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Viruses are acellular entities, meaning they do not have a cellular structure and lack cell membranes.
 
• They are composed of genetic material (either DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat called a capsid.
 
• Viruses cannot replicate on their own and must infect a host cell to reproduce.
 
• They do not possess organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, or ribosomes, which are found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Due to their lack of cellular structure, viruses are considered obligate intracellular parasites.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plant Cell**

 
 
• Plant cells have a cell wall, a large central vacuole, and chloroplasts in addition to the cell membrane.
 
• These cells are eukaryotic and have membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
 
• **Fungi Cell**
 
 
• Fungi cells are also eukaryotic and have a cell wall made of chitin, in addition to a cell membrane and membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
 
• **Animal Cell**
 
 
• Animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts but have a cell membrane and various membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain peaks is a part of the Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kamet** is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is a part of the **Himalayas** and specifically located in the Zanskar Range.
 
• Kamet stands at an elevation of **7,756 meters (25,446 feet)**.
 
• It is the third highest peak in India, outside of the Karakoram range.
 
• The peak was first summited in 1931 by Frank Smythe, Eric Shipton, and R.L. Holdsworth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The range has some of the planet's highest peaks, including the very highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.
 
• The Himalayas span five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan.
 
• The name "Himalaya" means "abode of snow" in Sanskrit, reflecting the vast amounts of snow and ice that cover the range.
 
 
 
• **Zanskar Range**
 
 
• The Zanskar Range is a mountain range in the union territory of Ladakh that separates Zanskar from Ladakh.
 
• It is a sub-range of the Himalayas and stretches from the eastern part of Ladakh to the Himachal Pradesh border.
 
• The range has many high peaks, with Kamet being one of the most prominent.
 
 
 
• **Mountaineering in India**
 
 
• India offers a variety of mountaineering opportunities, with the Himalayas being a prime destination.
 
• The Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) is the apex body for mountaineering and allied sports in India.
 
• Several high-altitude peaks in India are popular among climbers, including Nanda Devi, Kanchenjunga, and Kamet.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Conditions**
 
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in influencing the climate of the Indian subcontinent, particularly the monsoon.
 
• The high peaks block cold winds from Central Asia, keeping South Asia warmer in winter.
 
• The range also causes orographic precipitation, leading to diverse ecosystems and weather patterns across the region.

questions.question: Twinkling of stars is related to the phenomenon of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**refraction of light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The twinkling of stars is primarily caused by **refraction of light** as it passes through different layers of the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• As the light from a star enters the Earth's atmosphere, it gets bent multiple times due to varying air densities, resulting in a change of direction.
 
• This constant bending of light rays makes the stars appear to twinkle or flicker from our point of view on Earth.
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with different densities, such as from space (vacuum) into the Earth's atmosphere (air).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interference of Light**

 
 
• Interference is a phenomenon where two or more light waves superimpose to form a resultant wave of greater, lower, or the same amplitude.
 
• It is responsible for patterns such as fringes seen in experiments like the double-slit experiment.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Light**
 
 
• Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface back into the original medium.
 
• It is described by the law of reflection, which states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion of Light**
 
 
• Dispersion is the separation of light into its constituent colors due to different degrees of refraction for different wavelengths.
 
• This phenomenon is observed when light passes through a prism, creating a spectrum of colors.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can a member of the Public Service Commission be removed by the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 317**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 317** of the Indian Constitution deals with the removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission.
 
• A member of a Public Service Commission can be removed from office by the **President of India** based on certain conditions such as misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• The President can order an inquiry by the Supreme Court in cases of misbehavior.
 
• If the Supreme Court finds the member guilty, the President can remove the member from office.
 
• This provision ensures accountability and integrity within the Public Service Commissions in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Service Commission:**

 
 
• An independent constitutional body in India responsible for conducting exams and selecting candidates for various civil service positions.
 
• Examples include the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions.
 
 
 
• **Article 315:**
 
 
• It provides for the establishment of Public Service Commissions for the Union and for each state.
 
 
 
• **Article 316:**
 
 
• Deals with the appointment and term of office of members of the Public Service Commission.
 
• The Chairman and other members are appointed by the President (for UPSC) and by the Governor (for State PSCs).
 
 
 
• **Article 318:**
 
 
• Empowers the President to make rules regarding the number of members of the commission and their conditions of service.

questions.question: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shab-e-Barat is a significant Islamic observance that is celebrated by Muslims around the world.
 
• It is observed on the night between the 14th and 15th day of the Islamic month of Sha'ban.
 
• Muslims believe that on this night, God writes the destinies of all individuals for the coming year and forgives the sins of those who seek forgiveness.
 
• It is a night of prayer, reflection, and seeking forgiveness, often involving staying awake all night in devotion and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sha'ban**

 
 
• Sha'ban is the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
 
• It is considered a significant month for Muslims as it precedes the holy month of Ramadan.
 
• Many Muslims fast during this month and increase their worship in preparation for Ramadan.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Calendar**
 
 
• The Islamic calendar, also known as the Hijri calendar, is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 months in a year of 354 or 355 days.
 
• The calendar is used to determine the proper days of Islamic holidays and rituals, such as the annual period of fasting and the proper time for the pilgrimage to Mecca.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Prayer in Islam**
 
 
• Prayer, or Salah, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundation of a Muslim's faith and practice.
 
• It is a physical, mental, and spiritual act of worship that is observed five times every day at prescribed times.
 
• Prayers are performed facing the Kaaba in Mecca, and include specific recitations and movements.
 
 
 
• **Seeking Forgiveness in Islam**
 
 
• Seeking forgiveness, or Istighfar, is an important concept in Islam.
 
• Muslims believe that God is Merciful and Forgiving, and they regularly seek forgiveness for their sins and shortcomings.
 
• This practice is especially emphasized during significant nights such as Shab-e-Barat.

questions.question: Arrange the civilian awards in the ascending order of importance
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padmashri, Padmabhushan, Padmavibhushan, Bharat Ratna**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct order of civilian awards in ascending order of importance is **Padmashri, Padmabhushan, Padmavibhushan, Bharat Ratna**.
 
• The **Padma Awards** are one of the highest civilian honors of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (distinguished service of a high order), and **Padma Shri** (distinguished service).
 
• The **Bharat Ratna** is the highest civilian award of India, awarded for exceptional service towards the advancement of Art, Literature, and Science, and in recognition of Public Service of the highest order.
 
• The **Padma Awards** were instituted in 1954, while the **Bharat Ratna** was instituted in 1954 and is not limited to Indian citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Padma Awards** are announced every year on Republic Day and are conferred by the President of India in a ceremonial function held at Rashtrapati Bhawan.
 
• The awards are given in all disciplines/fields of activities, such as art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, civil service, etc.
 
• The **Bharat Ratna** awardees receive a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and a medallion. There is no monetary grant associated with the award.
 
• As of now, the **Bharat Ratna** has been awarded to 48 individuals, including 14 who were awarded posthumously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Bihu is the most important festival of Assam, celebrated thrice a year as Rongali Bihu, Kongali Bihu, and Bhogali Bihu.
 
• It is primarily an agricultural festival associated with the changing seasons.
 
• Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April to mark the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.
 
• Kongali Bihu is observed in October and is a solemn occasion with less merrymaking.
 
• Bhogali Bihu, celebrated in January, marks the end of the harvest season and is characterized by feasts and bonfires.

• Rongker is usually observed in the month of April or May.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used for the estimation of poverty in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Head Count Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Head Count Ratio (HCR) is a measure used to estimate the proportion of a population living below the poverty line.
 
• In India, the poverty line is determined based on consumption expenditure, which is assessed periodically through surveys conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO).
 
• HCR is expressed as the percentage of the population whose income or consumption levels fall below a defined threshold (poverty line).
 
• This method helps in identifying the proportion of people who are unable to meet their basic consumption needs, thereby providing insights into the extent of poverty in a region.
 
• The planning commission and now NITI Aayog use the HCR in conjunction with other metrics to shape poverty alleviation policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Absolute Poverty**

 
 
• Refers to a condition where an individual lacks the financial resources to meet basic needs such as food, clothing, and shelter.
 
• It is measured against a fixed threshold, often termed as the poverty line.
 
• In India, absolute poverty is often evaluated using calorie intake-based poverty lines.
 
 
 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**
 
 
• Developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• It measures poverty by considering multiple deprivations in health, education, and living standards.
 
• MPI is more comprehensive than single-dimension measures like income or consumption.
 
 
 
• **Relative Poverty**
 
 
• Relative poverty measures an individual's or a group's economic status relative to the rest of society.
 
• It focuses on inequality and the distribution of income within a population.
 
• Relative poverty thresholds are often set at a percentage of median income.
 
 
 
• **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**
 
 
• The NSSO is responsible for conducting large-scale surveys to collect data on various socio-economic indicators.
 
• It plays a crucial role in gathering data used for poverty estimation in India.
 
• Founded in 1950, it operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?

__
 
• **Non-tax revenue** refers to the recurring income earned by the government from sources other than taxes.
 
• Fees and fines are common examples of non-tax revenue. **Fees** are payments made to the government for specific services or activities (e.g., passport fees, court fees), while **fines** are penalties imposed for violating laws or regulations.
 
• Non-tax revenue sources help the government fund its operations without increasing the tax burden on citizens.
 
• Other examples of non-tax revenue include **interest receipts** on loans given by the government, **dividends** from public sector enterprises, and income from government property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a significant source of revenue for the government and is also a direct tax.
 
 
 
• **Value-added tax (VAT):**

• Consumers ultimately bear the cost of VAT as it is included in the purchase price of goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Non-tax revenue sources:**

• Examples include fees for services, fines and penalties, dividends from public enterprises, interest receipts, and revenue from government properties.

questions.question: Why was the Brahmi script used in Ashoka's inscriptions important for modern India?

options.text: It formed the basis for many modern Indian scripts
It was used in the Mauryan military manuals
It was restricted only to religious texts
It influenced the development of Chinese characters

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - It formed the basis for many modern Indian scripts**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmi Script**

 
 
• The Brahmi script is one of the oldest writing systems in the Indian subcontinent, dating back to the 3rd century BCE.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions, which were written in Brahmi, played a key role in the script's dissemination and standardization.
 
• This script evolved into numerous modern Indian scripts, including Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Bengali.
 
• The decipherment of Brahmi provided crucial insights into ancient Indian history and linguistics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mauryan Military Manuals**

 
 
• While the Mauryan Empire did have military manuals, they were not specifically associated with the Brahmi script.
 
• Military manuals were more likely to be oral traditions or written in other contemporary scripts.
 
 
 
• **Religious Texts**
 
 
• Brahmi script was used for a wide range of texts including administrative and legal documents, not just religious texts.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions included edicts on governance, ethics, and social welfare, extending beyond religious content.
 
 
 
• **Chinese Characters**
 
 
• Chinese characters developed independently and were not influenced by the Brahmi script.
 
• The evolution of Chinese writing is a separate linguistic tradition with different origins and influences.

questions.question: Which of the following are called as 'chloroplasts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Green pigmented plastids**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green pigmented plastids** are referred to as chloroplasts.
 
• Chloroplasts are essential organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis.
 
• These plastids contain the green pigment **chlorophyll**, which is crucial for capturing light energy.
 
• Chloroplasts convert light energy into chemical energy through the process of photosynthesis, producing oxygen and glucose as byproducts.
 
• They play a significant role in the energy cycle of plants and are vital for their growth and survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chloroplasts are believed to have originated from cyanobacteria through a process called **endosymbiosis**.
 
• They have their own **DNA** and ribosomes, which are similar to those of cyanobacteria, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
 
• Chloroplasts are surrounded by a double membrane and contain internal structures called **thylakoids**, where the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur.
 
• The **stroma** is the fluid-filled space surrounding the thylakoids, where the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) take place.
 
• In addition to chlorophyll, chloroplasts also contain other pigments like **carotenoids** that assist in photosynthesis by capturing additional light wavelengths.

questions.question: We observe geometrical shadow of an opaque object when light is incident on it. This is due to __________.

options.text: dispersion of the light by an object
light travelling in a straight line

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**light travelling in a straight line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The geometrical shadow is formed because light travels in straight lines.
 
• When an opaque object blocks the path of light, it prevents the light from reaching a certain area, creating a shadow.
 
• The sharpness of the shadow depends on the size of the light source and the distance between the object and the surface where the shadow is formed.
 
• Diffraction, dispersion, and reflection of light do not contribute to the formation of a geometrical shadow.
 
• Geometrical shadows are a common observation in everyday life, such as the shadow of a person on a sunny day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of light waves around obstacles or through small openings.
 
• This phenomenon is more noticeable when the size of the obstacle or opening is comparable to the wavelength of the light.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion**
 
 
• Dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colors when it passes through a prism.
 
• This occurs because different colors of light have different refractive indices in the prism material.
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• Reflection is the bouncing back of light rays when they hit a smooth surface, like a mirror.
 
• The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection in the case of a smooth reflective surface.

questions.question: The Morley-Minto Reforms, also known as the Indian Councils Act of 1909, introduced which significant feature into Indian legislative councils?

• This statement is **correct** as a significant feature of the Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act of 1909).

• This was a major development in the political landscape of colonial India and marked the beginning of communal representation in Indian politics.

• This option is **incorrect** because competitive exams were introduced for civil services under the Charter Act of 1853, not the Indian Councils Act of 1909.
 
 
 
• **Complete self-government for provinces**
 
 
• This option is **incorrect** as the Morley-Minto Reforms did not grant complete self-government. Provincial autonomy was introduced gradually, with the Government of India Act of 1935 providing a greater level of self-governance.

• Expanded legislative councils, although the powers of Indian members remained limited.

questions.question: The conservation of linear momentum leads to Newton's

options.text: Not related to any newton's law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third law.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion** states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. This is directly related to the **conservation of linear momentum** in a system where no external forces act.
 
• The principle of conservation of linear momentum arises from the fact that the **total momentum before and after an interaction remains constant** if no external force is applied.
 
• In an isolated system, the action and reaction forces between two objects are **equal in magnitude and opposite in direction**, ensuring the momentum of the system remains conserved. 
 
• For example, in a collision (elastic or inelastic), the total momentum of the system before the collision equals the total momentum after the collision, demonstrating the applicability of the Third Law.
 
• *Hence, the conservation of linear momentum is directly related to **Newton’s Third Law of Motion**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• **First Law (Law of Inertia):** A body remains in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. This explains the concept of inertia.
 
• **Second Law:** The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the direction of the force. Mathematically, *F = ma*, where *F* is force, *m* is mass, and *a* is acceleration.
 
• **Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. It implies forces always occur in pairs.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Linear Momentum:**
 
 
• The **law of conservation of linear momentum** states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external forces act on it.
 
• It is mathematically expressed as: *m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂*, where *m* is mass, *u* is initial velocity, and *v* is final velocity.
 
• This principle is widely applied in areas like collisions, rocket propulsion, and explosions.
 
 
 
• **Examples of the Third Law and Momentum Conservation:**
 
 
• When a gun is fired, the bullet moves forward (action) and the gun recoils backward (reaction). The momentum of the bullet and the gun are equal and opposite, conserving the total momentum.
 
• Rocket propulsion works based on this principle. The ejection of exhaust gases (action) creates an equal and opposite force propelling the rocket forward (reaction).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relation Between Newton's Third Law and Momentum Conservation:**

 
 
• The equal and opposite forces described by the Third Law ensure that any change in momentum of one object is counterbalanced by an equal and opposite change in momentum of the other object, leading to conservation.
 
• This relationship is crucial in analyzing systems like collisions, where no external force acts.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Real Life:**
 
 
• Understanding vehicle collisions and safety mechanisms like airbags.
 
• Explaining the working of jet engines and rockets.
 
• Analysis of sports actions like hitting a ball with a bat or swimming.

• **Amendment of the Constitution**
 
 
• The procedure for the amendment of the Constitution is laid down in Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution.
 
• It provides for a flexible procedure for the amendment to address the changing needs and circumstances of the country.
 
• An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament and must be passed by a special majority.
 
 
 
• **National Emergency**
 
 
• National emergency provisions are contained in Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A National Emergency can be declared on the grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• During a National Emergency, the federal structure of the country changes to a unitary one, and the central government becomes more powerful.
